title: WEGOVY (semaglutide) injection, for subcutaneous use; WEGOVY (semaglutide) tablets, for oral use: full prescribing information
journal: US Food and Drug Administration; DailyMed, US National Library of Medicine, set id ee06186f-2aa3-4990-a760-757579d8f77b, version 19, effective 18 June 2026
result: Indications: reduction of major adverse cardiovascular events in adults with established cardiovascular disease and obesity or overweight; chronic weight management in adults with BMI of 30 kg/m2 or more, or 27 or more with a weight-related comorbidity, and in patients aged 12 years and older with obesity; non-cirrhotic MASH with F2 to F3 fibrosis under accelerated approval. Recent major changes: Suicidal Behavior and Ideation (5.10) removed 02/2026. Boxed warning for thyroid C-cell tumours as for Ozempic. Cholelithiasis 1.6% against 0.7% on placebo injection and cholecystitis 0.6% against 0.2% in adults; in adolescents cholelithiasis 3.8% and cholecystitis 0.8% against 0%; gallbladder disease exceeded placebo even after accounting for the degree of weight loss. Severe gastrointestinal reactions 4.1% against 0.9%; gastrointestinal reactions 73% against 47%, leading to permanent discontinuation in 4.3% against 0.7%. Adjudicated acute pancreatitis in 4 patients (0.2 per 100 patient-years) against 1 (under 0.1). Acute kidney injury 0.4 against 0.2 cases per 100 patient-years, more frequent with prior renal impairment and during titration. Hypotension 1.3% against 0.4% and syncope 0.8% against 0.2%. Appendicitis 10 (0.5%) against 2 (0.2%). Resting heart rate rose 1 to 4 beats per minute; maximum rises of 20 beats per minute or more at any visit in 26% against 16% of adults and 54% against 39% of adolescents. Hypoglycaemia below 54 mg/dL in type 2 diabetes 6.2% against 2.5%; in trials without diabetes hypoglycaemia was not systematically captured; in SELECT serious hypoglycaemia occurred in 2 of 87 patients with prior bariatric surgery on semaglutide against 0 of 97 on placebo. SELECT: 8803 patients exposed for a median 37.3 months and 8801 for 38.6 months; safety data collection was limited to serious adverse events, adverse events leading to discontinuation and adverse events of special interest; 16% against 8% stopped for an adverse event; hip and pelvis fractures in women 24 of 2448 (1%) against 5 of 2424 (0.2%) and at age 75 or more 17 of 703 (2.4%) against 4 of 663 (0.6%); urolithiasis 1.2% against 0.8%. MASH trial fractures 4.4% (2.6 per 100 patient-years) against 3.3% (2.0). The 7.2 mg dose caused dysaesthesia in 22% against 6% on 2.4 mg and 0.3% on placebo, unresolved during the trial in 18% of those affected. Weight-reduction Study 5 (STEP 4) randomised 803 of 902 patients after a 20-week run-in in which 99 (11%) stopped, 48 (5.3%) for adverse reactions; the label states its results may not reflect patients first starting the drug. Postmarketing: necrotising pancreatitis sometimes resulting in death, ileus, intestinal obstruction, faecal impaction, pulmonary aspiration during anaesthesia, acute kidney injury. Oral tablets raised levothyroxine exposure by 33%. Semaglutide lowers body weight with greater fat mass loss than lean mass loss. Discontinue when pregnancy is recognised and at least 2 months before a planned pregnancy.
